newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan stocks end higher on Bhutto dismissal.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan stocks end higher on Bhutto dismissal.

text.p: Pakistani stocks briefly notched their biggest gains of the year on Wednesday in reaction to the sacking of Benazir Bhutto's government, dealers said.
Karachi's 100-share index surged nearly 110 points to 1,607.84 before profit-taking kicked in later in the session. It closed 78.63 points or 5.25 percent higher at 1,577.40.
The intra-day climb was the biggest one-day leap in the index this year, surpassing a 66.6-point rise on March 28, dealers said.
"The market overreacted to the government's dismissal and profit-taking trimmed the early gains," one dealer said.
"But overall market senitment is positive after the removal of Bhutto's government."
Bhutto was dismissed on Tuesday for a second time in her turbulent political career by president Farooq Leghari, who accused her beleaguered government of corruption, nepotism and misrule.
"People are bullish since the government was removed yesterday," dealer Khalid Waheed said.
"Prices soared in Tuesday's kerb trading and that rally continues. But this sharp rise can prove dangerous because speculators dominate trading."
Gainers led losers 262 to 16. Pak State oil rose 20 rupees to 400 and Dewan Salman Fibres 1.90 to 40.30.
The Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry said on Tuesday it hoped President Farooq Leghari's dismissal of Benazir Bhutto's government would augur well for the battered economy.
"The president's decision, though quite late, has finally ended the uncertainty on the political front," the federation's president Senator Ilyas Bilour told reporters in Karachi.
Bilour said Leghari's action was likely to improve investor confidence, whatever the political implications.

He urged the new caretaker government led by Meraj Khalid to prosecute corrupt businessmen, bureaucrats and politicians, restore the credibility of institutions, and sack government employees appointed on political grounds.
"Corruption and over-employment was a burden on the economy. The new set-up should rectify the situation to restore confidence among businessmen," he said.
Pakistan's new caretaker government purged the bureaucracy of senior officials but its lawyers denied on Wednesday the administration had placed Bhutto under house arrest.
Interim Prime Minister Meraj Khalid and his nine ministers were set to hold their first cabinet meeting on Wednesday.
